fields.subnational_unit: Gondar City, Amhara Region (Angereb Reservoir, groundwater wells and springs)
fields.sample_size: 168 monthly supply observations (January 2011 - March 2024) from the Gondar City Water Supply and Sanitation Service plus monthly rainfall and temperature; qualitative phase 15-20 April 2024: six key informant interviews and four focus groups (24 participants in total, purposively selected)
fields.effect_measure: Mann-Kendall and Sen's slope trend tests, Pettitt/PELT/CUSUM change-point detection, SPI and lagged rainfall correlations, with inductive thematic analysis of interviews and focus groups
fields.covariates: monthly rainfall (SPI) and temperature as climate variables; no household covariates
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: MMAT (re-appraised 2026-10-04 on the full text; supersedes the abstract-only rating of 2026-09-28). S1=Yes; S2=Yes. Mixed-methods criteria: 5.1(rationale)=Yes (sequential explanatory design justified); 5.2(integration)=Yes (statistical change points interpreted through stakeholder accounts, Figure 2); 5.3(meta-inference)=Yes ('integrated insight': more production but unchanged household access); 5.4(divergence)=Yes (the gap between aggregate supply growth and residents' experience is analysed); 5.5(component quality)=Yes (14 years of records with a stated data-quality cut-off, serial-correlation correction, three-stage coding, triangulation; purposive sample of 24 and a single city). Per MMAT's own guide, no composite score is computed.
fields.section: Full text (Scientific Reports, open-access web version): Abstract; Introduction; Materials and methods; Results; Discussion; Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Abstract; research design p3; data collection and analysis p3-5; results trends and change points; thematic analysis (five themes)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a sequential explanatory mixed-methods analysis of Gondar City, Ethiopia, water supply (168 monthly records 2011-2024; 24 interview and focus-group participants) read in full text 2026-10-04 (open-access web version). Groundwater and spring supply rose significantly (Mann-Kendall) with identifiable change points while reservoir output stayed flat; residents report no improvement at the tap because of distribution losses and population growth; management described as reactive. Utility operations rather than a legal or administrative access rule.
pdf_note: Scientific Reports article web print (2026), about 88,000 characters read; figure and table images not read
notes: Operational time-series with qualitative interpretation; the legal/administrative content is weak (reactive management, no strategic plan).
